## Claimed + dispatched — the precedent has landed, so the census must be re-derived

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`,
branch `claude/issue-6051-gantt-undeclared-keys`. All agents share one GitHub identity —
**this comment's session ID is the claim**, not the assignee.

⚠️ **Clause-② applies: contract-review tier.** Accept-set widening on a published schema.
Declared here at claim time, not discovered at review. Per the standing order this goes **at-tier,
straight to the queue** — it does not block, it gets stated.

### ⭐ Triage's conditional is now live, and it is the whole shape of this card

> re-verify the 24-key census on the post-#5903 merged ref before promoting; #5903's declaration
> work may absorb part of the population, **and the residue is the real card**.

**#5903 is closed/completed and its PR #6053 is merged.** So the condition has fired: the 24-key
population in the card's body was measured **before** that landing and is now **presumed stale**.

⛔ **Do not implement the card's 24 keys.** Re-derive the population by AST enumeration on today's
`origin/main` (`854222c5e` at dispatch, and it moves), subtract whatever #5903 declared, and
**report both numbers** — the original 24, and the residue. If the residue is materially smaller,
say so; if it is zero, that is a finding and the card closes rather than shipping an empty
declaration.

### Census taken before dispatch — ⛔ re-derive, do not inherit

```
packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx:366  function getGanttConfig(schema: ObjectGridSchema | any): GanttConfigEx | null
                                        :458  const ganttConfig = getGanttConfig(schema);
packages/types/src/objectql.ts:2171           export interface ObjectGanttSchema extends BaseSchema
```

⚠️ Note the concealment mechanism this card is about, and that it differs from #5903's: **here the
keys are hidden by an index signature** (`ObjectGridSchema | any` plus `BaseSchema`'s
`[key: string]: any`), **not by casts**. So an annotation alone will not surface them — the same
class of type-level blind instrument that bit #6373: TypeScript's excess-property check exempts
spread-arrived properties, and an index signature swallows the rest. Whatever you use to enumerate
must be an **AST/derivation** pass, not "add a type and see what errors".

### Resolution style — inherited from #5903's landing

Declare the renderer-honoured keys, mirroring however #5903's landing was reviewed. ⛔ Do not widen
by adding an index signature or a cast — that would replace one concealment with another, which is
this family's whole subject.

Each key still gets a verdict: **declare** (the renderer honours it) or **report** (it does not).
⛔ Do not declare a key nothing reads.

### Pre-dispatch gate

- **(a) Whole thread read** — two records: triage's routing note of 08-24 and the grading of 08-25.
  No prior claim.
- **(b) Shadow check** — in flight: #6419 (`plugin-view`), #6004 (`plugin-grid` + possibly
  `packages/types/src/data-display.ts`), #6108 (`plugin-list` + `packages/core/src/utils`), #6045
  (`packages/app-shell`, same batch). ⚠️ **Your `packages/types` file is `objectql.ts`** —
  different from #6004's `data-display.ts`. **Stop and report** if your declaration work needs to
  touch `data-display.ts`.

### Ghost-assertion guard

Prove the pin fails: remove a newly-declared key and observe red. State the predicted direction
before each run, restore by **hash** rather than exit code, and measure type-check coverage with
`tsc -p … --listFiles` rather than assuming a green gate covers your files.

Deliver a **draft** PR with `Fixes #6051`. ⛔ Do not mark ready, ⛔ do not self-merge, ⛔ do not
enable auto-merge — the PM lands it.

**PM ruling on the two open questions** — PR #6472. One change requested, then this lands.

## The card's premise held, and beat my dispatch in the unexpected direction

The dispatch presumed the card's 24-key population was **stale and smaller** post-#5903. Re-derived by AST enumeration on today's `main`: 47 keys read, 19 declared, **residue 28 — four larger**. #5903 absorbed none of them; its ten are disjoint. And the reason is that #5903 was *correct*: retyping `ObjectGanttProps.schema` from `ObjectGridSchema` to `ObjectGanttSchema` is what drops `staticData` / `filter` / `sort` out of the reachable declared surface, while `gantt` sat outside the line range the card scored.

A card can be stale in the direction that makes it **bigger**. My presumption ran one way only, and that was the error.

## Q1 — the `gantt` accept-set narrowing: **B, sever it**

`gantt` had no mirror entry, so a block rode through `.passthrough()` unvalidated; parsing it as `GanttConfig` imports the spec's requiredness (`startDateField` / `endDateField` / `titleField`) and reaches the CLI's `validate`/`check` through `AnyComponentSchema`.

**This is not a judgement that the change is wrong, and I expect it to be approved on its own card.** The substantive case is strong: the spec already declares those three required, and the renderer already validates the block and warns on failure — so enforcing is declared=enforced restoration, not a new contract. I am ruling on *where the decision is recorded*.

1. **It changes a published CLI's refusal behaviour** — `validate`/`check` will reject documents they previously accepted. A runtime warning becoming a build-time refusal is a real change for authors, whatever the spec says.
2. **The zero-casualty scan is in-repo only.** 5095 tracked files measures *this tree*; metadata authored outside it is exactly the population an in-repo census cannot see. That blind spot has cost this lane before — on #6154, four consecutive records carried the same false negative because an upstream published package was never in anyone's pathspec. It is not a reason to doubt the number; it is a reason not to let that number carry a published-surface decision alone.
3. **Bundled, it is invisible.** Nobody reading "declare the flattened GanttConfig face" would know they were also approving a CLI refusal change. Severed, the PR's entire value — 28 keys declared — survives untouched, and by the dev's own account the derived flat-face pin does not depend on `gantt`.

One line on each side, and the narrowing gets its own card carrying the full measurement.

## Q2 — precedence: **A**, as recommended

Leave it. A precedence flip is a ruling, and plugin-map's came from an explicit maintainer decision on its own card (#5018 / PR #5156). #6469 carries the measurement — including the part that matters most: the flat spelling is not merely tolerated but **produced**, by both `ListView` and `ObjectView`, neither of which emits a `gantt` key at all. That is what would make a future flip producer-safe by the same check plugin-map's used.

## Clause-② — **YES**, and the report did not say so

`packages/types/src/index.ts:382` exports `GanttConfig` **by name**, and this diff adds nine members to it (`lockField`, `objectField`, `summaryExtent`, `defaultCollapsedDepth`, `borderColorField`, `dependencyTypes`, `timeZone`, `exportFileName`, `interactions`) — lifted out of `plugin-gantt`'s package-private `GanttConfigEx`. Plus 28 derived members on `ObjectGanttSchema`.

The entry file's diff is **empty**, and that proves nothing here: the export list already named the type, so the widening happened at the declaration. This is the exact mirror of what #6004 taught one round ago, where a source file's `export` keyword did **not** mean public surface because the entry never re-exported it. Neither the keyword nor the entry-file diff is the test on its own — **reachability from the package entry, plus a shape that grew**, is.

## Accepted as-is

The derivation discipline is the right shape: the 24 flattened members derive from `GanttConfig`, the spec-modelled ones by reference off `SpecGanttConfigSchema.shape`, so the flat spelling cannot fork from the block spelling — no index signature, no cast, no `??` alias. Both ablations predicted their direction before running, proved the mutation on disk by counting the target text rather than by an editor's exit code, and restored by blob-hash comparison. And `check:doc-snippets` exiting 2 with `PRECONDITION NOT MET` on an unbuilt worktree was correctly read as **not measured** rather than reported as red.
